findings.source_quote: οὐδὲ ὅταν θέλῃ ἄνθρωπος λαλεῖν, λαλεῖ τὸ πνεῦμα τὸ ἅγιον
findings.english_quote: nor does the holy Spirit speak whenever a person wishes it to speak
findings.issue: The Greek makes the person the subject of wishing to speak. The English instead makes the person's wish concern the Spirit's speaking, changing the expressed contrast between human willingness to speak and divine initiative.
findings.suggested_revision: Proposed for fresh review: “nor does the holy Spirit speak whenever a person wishes to speak.” Retain the following statement that it speaks when God wishes the man to speak.

findings.source_quote: οὕτω καὶ τὰ πνεύματα τὰ ἐπίγεια ἀδύνατά ἐστι καὶ ἀδρανῆ
findings.english_quote: so also the spirits that are earthly are impossible and inert.
findings.issue: Here ἀδύνατα describes the earthly spirits as lacking ability or power, not as impossible entities. “Are impossible” obscures the assertion being made about them. The repeated Greek word links impossible feats with powerless spirits, but its English sense must follow its subject.
findings.suggested_revision: Proposed for fresh review: “so also earthly spirits are powerless and inactive.” A brief note can preserve the repeated Greek word connecting impossibility and inability.

findings.english_quote: Project default prefers “slaves” where belonging to God is salient; Hermas emphasizes divine ownership.
findings.issue: The lexical metadata falsely states the current project default and records “slaves (of God)” as chosen, while the reader text correctly uses “servants of God.” The theological metadata repeats the same policy contradiction.
findings.suggested_revision: Update both metadata blocks to record the actual chosen reader wording, “servants of God,” and the current servant policy. Preserve bonded status, belonging, and allegiance as explanatory nuance rather than claiming a slave default.

findings.source_quote: ὅσοι δὲ δίψυχοί εἰσι καὶ πυκνῶς μετανοοῦσι, μαντεύονται ὡς καὶ τὰ ἔθνη
findings.english_quote: Retain change their minds: this is retreat from baptism or vacillation into divination, not repentance toward God.
findings.issue: The note and metadata introduce “retreat from baptism,” which is not stated in the selected passage. The supplied repair report preserves the prior decision but supplies no textual argument establishing that baptismal identification. The adverse vacillation reading need not be replaced, but this added specificity is unsupported here.
findings.suggested_revision: Retain the disclosed contextual “change their minds” reading provisionally. Explain its connection with double-mindedness and divination without asserting retreat from baptism, or supply a bounded source-based argument and label that identification as interpretation.

findings.issue: The theological metadata identifies “faith from the divine Spirit” and “spirit-given faith” as plausible alternatives to the selected objective-genitive reading, but no reader-facing footnote preserves those alternatives. Footnote e concerns a different textual choice.
findings.suggested_revision: Keep the selected “faith in the divine Spirit” reading and add a concise footnote identifying the alternative source reading, such as “Or: faith from the divine Spirit.” Review the proposed note before publication.

findings.source_quote: οὐδὲ ὅταν θέλῃ ἄνθρωπος λαλεῖν, λαλεῖ τὸ πνεῦμα τὸ ἅγιον
findings.english_quote: The holy Spirit does not speak whenever a person wants.
findings.issue: The simplified wording omits what the person wants to do: speak. In context it can instead suggest that the person wants the Spirit to speak, inheriting the standard edition's altered agency rather than independently preserving the Greek clause.
findings.suggested_revision: Proposed for fresh review: “The holy Spirit does not speak whenever a person wants to speak.” Preserve the following God-directed condition.

findings.source_quote: εἶτα ὅλως εἰς συναγωγὴν ἀνδρῶν δικαίων οὐκ ἐγγίζει, ἀλλ' ἀποφεύγει αὐτούς.
findings.english_quote: He avoids gatherings of righteous men.
findings.issue: This collapses two assertions into general avoidance and loses the emphatic negative assertion that he does not approach such a gathering at all. The difficult juxtaposition with his entering a gathering in paragraph 14 should not be softened.
findings.suggested_revision: Proposed for fresh review: “He does not go near a gathering of righteous men at all. Instead, he avoids them.”

findings.source_quote: πρῶτον μὲν ὁ ἔχων τὸ πνεῦμα [τὸ θεῖον] τὸ ἄνωθεν
findings.english_quote: First, the man with the divine spirit from above
findings.issue: The simplified edition presents “divine” without identifying its bracketed editorial status in the working source. Unlike the standard edition's “[divine],” neither this wording nor an accompanying note distinguishes the supplement from unbracketed text.
findings.suggested_revision: Retain the working wording but mark “[divine]” or add a reader-facing note stating that “divine” is bracketed in the selected edition. Do not treat the supplement as newly verified manuscript text.

findings.english_quote: Project default prefers “slaves” where belonging to God is salient; Hermas emphasizes divine ownership.
findings.issue: The simplified edition's lexical and theological metadata claim a slave default and record slave wording as chosen, although its own reader text correctly says “God’s servants.” This contradicts both the edition and current policy.
findings.suggested_revision: Record “God’s servants” as this edition's chosen wording. Correct the policy description and preserve bonded-status and ownership nuance in explanatory metadata without changing the reader text to “slaves.”

findings.source_quote: ὅσοι δὲ δίψυχοί εἰσι καὶ πυκνῶς μετανοοῦσι, μαντεύονται ὡς καὶ τὰ ἔθνη
findings.english_quote: Retain change their minds: this is retreat from baptism or vacillation into divination, not repentance toward God.
findings.issue: The simplified edition independently repeats an unsupported baptismal identification in its note and metadata. The selected clause connects frequent changes of mind with double-mindedness and divination but does not mention baptism.
findings.suggested_revision: Keep the contextual adverse-change reading provisionally, but remove the asserted baptismal identification or document a source-based argument and explicitly distinguish interpretation from translation.

findings.english_quote: who have faith in the divine Spirit
findings.issue: The edition chooses the objective-genitive interpretation while its metadata recognizes plausible source-genitive alternatives. Those alternatives are not preserved in a reader-facing footnote as current policy requires.
findings.suggested_revision: Retain the selected reading and propose a concise footnote, such as “Or: faith from the divine Spirit,” for fresh review.

summary: Both editions require revision after separate review against the selected twenty-one-paragraph Greek source. The standard edition changes human speaking agency in paragraph 8 and misrenders the earthly spirits' powerlessness in paragraph 19; the simplified edition also weakens paragraph 13's emphatic negation and conceals a bracketed supplement. Both carry contradictory servant-policy metadata, unsupported baptismal specificity, and an undisclosed reader-facing genitive alternative. The substantive reported textual alternatives are otherwise adequately attributed to mediated project evidence; retaining the disclosed working readings is not itself a defect. This review does not authenticate unseen manuscripts or certify exhaustive collation. All proposed corrections require fresh review.
